Mesillat Yesharim 11:94: And the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 55a): the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth. And certainly, if truth is what the Holy One, blessed be He, chose to take as His own seal, how abominable its opposite must be before Him.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:95: And the Holy One, blessed be He, gave great warning concerning truth, saying (Zechariah 8:16): "Speak the truth every man with his neighbor." And He said (Isaiah 16:5): "and a throne shall be established in kindness, and he shall sit upon it in truth." And He said (ibid. 63:8): "And He said, Surely they are My people, children that will not deal falsely." Behold, thus you learn that the one depends on the other.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:96: And He said (Zechariah 8:3): "and Jerusalem shall be called the city of truth," to magnify its importance. And the Sages, of blessed memory, have already said (Makkot 24a): "and speaks truth in his heart" — this refers to one such as Rav Safra, etc. — to make known to you how far the obligation of truth extends.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:97: And they have already forbidden a Torah scholar from departing from his own word, except in three matters.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:98: And one of the pillars upon which the world stands is truth; if so, whoever speaks falsehood is as though he removed the very foundation of the world, and conversely, whoever is careful with truth is as though he upholds the foundation of the world.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:99: And the Sages, of blessed memory, already told (Sanhedrin 97a) of a certain place whose people were so careful with truth that the Angel of Death had no power there; and because the wife of a certain rabbi altered her words, even though her intention was good, she thereby aroused the Angel of Death among them, until they expelled her from there because of this, and returned to their tranquility.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:100: And there is no need to elaborate on this matter, for reason obligates it and understanding compels it.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:101: The branches of the desecration of God's Name are also numerous and great, for a person must be very much concerned for the honor of his Maker, and in whatever he does he must look and reflect very carefully so that nothing should emerge from it that could be a desecration of the honor of Heaven, God forbid.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:102: And we have already learned: whether unwitting or deliberate, both are considered desecration of the Name.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:103: And they said, of blessed memory (Yoma 86a): What is an example of desecration of the Name? Rav said: such as I, who take meat and do not pay for it immediately. And Rabbi Yochanan said: such as I, who walk four cubits without words of Torah and without tefillin.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:104: And the matter is that every person, according to his own level and according to how he is regarded in the eyes of his generation, must take care not to do anything unbecoming a person of his standing; for the greater his importance and his wisdom, the more his watchfulness in matters of service and his exactitude in it should increase — and if he does not do so, the Name of Heaven is desecrated through him, God forbid, for it is the honor of the Torah that whoever increases his study of it should likewise increase his integrity and the improvement of his character traits; and whatever is lacking in this regard for one who increases in study causes disgrace to the study itself, and this, God forbid, is a desecration of His Name, blessed be He, who gave us His holy Torah and commanded us to engage in it in order to attain our perfection through it.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:105: And the observance of Sabbaths and festivals is also extensive, for its laws are many, and so they said (Shabbat 12a): "there is a great body of law regarding the Sabbath."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:106: And even matters of rabbinic rest, although they are of rabbinic origin, are fundamental; and so they said (Chagigah 16b): never let a matter of rabbinic rest be light in your eyes, for behold, laying on of hands is a matter of rabbinic rest, and yet the great ones of the generation disputed over it.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:107: However, the particulars of these laws in their divisions are explained by the decisors in their books, and they are all equally our obligation and require the same watchfulness. And what is difficult for the masses to observe is ceasing from business and from speaking of their commercial dealings; but this prohibition is explained in the words of the prophet (Isaiah 58:13): "and shall honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own business, nor speaking of matters" (Shabbat 150a). And the rule is: whatever is forbidden to do on the Sabbath is forbidden to strive after or to speak of with one's mouth.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:108: And therefore they forbade examining one's assets to see what is needed for the next day (Eruvin 38b), or going to the city gate in order to leave quickly for the bathhouse when the Sabbath ends. And they forbade saying, "I will do such-and-such tomorrow," or "I will buy such-and-such merchandise tomorrow," and so on with all similar things.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:109: Now, up to this point I have spoken of a few of the commandments in which we see that people commonly stumble, and from these we may learn regarding all the other negative commandments — for there is no prohibition that does not have branches and particulars, some of them severe and some light, and whoever wishes to be clean must be clean of all of them and pure of all of them.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:110: And the Sages, of blessed memory, have already said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6): "Your teeth are like a flock of ewes" — just as this ewe is modest, so Israel were modest and fit during the war with Midian. Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Acha: that not one of them put on the head-tefillin before the hand-tefillin — for had even one of them done so first, Moses would not have praised them, and they would not have emerged from there in peace.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:111: And so they said in the Yerushalmi: whoever converses between the blessing "Yishtabach" and the blessing "Yotzer" has a transgression in his hand, and it is counted against him among those who are exempted from military service.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:112: Behold, then, how far genuine exactitude and cleanliness in one's deeds must reach.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:113: Now, just as cleanliness is required in one's deeds, so cleanliness is required in one's character traits, and cleanliness in character traits is nearly more difficult than in deeds, for nature operates more powerfully in character traits than it does in deeds, since one's temperament and constitution either greatly assist or greatly oppose them; and every battle that goes against the inclination of one's nature is a mighty battle. This is what they explained in their statement, of blessed memory (Avot 4:1): "Who is mighty? He who conquers his inclination."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:114: Now, character traits are numerous, for corresponding to all the activities that pertain to a person in the world are the traits that he follows in his actions.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:115: However, just as we spoke of the commandments in which there was greater need to become clean — namely, those in which people commonly tend to stumble — so we will speak of the principal character traits at greater length, because of our familiarity with them, and they are: pride, anger, envy, and desire.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:116: Behold, all these are bad traits whose evil is recognized and well known, needing no proofs, for they are evil in themselves and evil in their consequences, for they all run counter to reason and wisdom, and each one alone is enough to bring a person to grave transgressions.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:117: Concerning pride, Scripture explicitly warns and says (Deuteronomy 8:14): "and your heart grows haughty, and you forget the Lord your God."
Mesillat Yesharim 11:118: Concerning anger, our Sages, of blessed memory, said: whoever becomes angry should be in your eyes as though he worshiped idols.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:119: Concerning envy and desire, we learned explicitly (Avot 4:21): envy, desire, and the pursuit of honor drive a person out of the world.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:120: However, the reflection required regarding them is how to escape them and all their branches, for they are all, together, offshoots of a foreign vine. Let us begin to speak of them, one by one.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:121: The general matter of pride is this: that a person esteems himself, and imagines in his heart that praise is fitting for him.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:122: And indeed, this can arise from many different opinions, for there is one who considers himself intelligent, one who considers himself handsome, one who considers himself honorable, one who considers himself great, and one who considers himself wise. In sum: any one of the good things in the world, if a person thinks that he possesses it, he is immediately at risk of falling into this pit of pride.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:123: But once a person has fixed in his heart that he is important and deserving of praise, the consequence arising from this thought will not be only one, but many varied consequences will arise from it, and even opposite ones may be found among them, born of one and the same cause, both aiming at the same thing.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:124: Behold, one proud man will be found who thinks in his heart that, since he is deserving of praise and is distinguished and marked out by his rank as he perceives it, it is fitting that he too should conduct himself in a distinguished and marked manner with great honor — whether in his walking, his sitting, his rising, his speech, and in all his deeds; he will only walk with great deliberateness, his heel beside his greatness; he will only sit reclining; he will only rise slowly, little by little, like a serpent,
Mesillat Yesharim 11:125: he will speak with no one except the honorable of the people, and even among them he will speak only in short pronouncements, like the sayings of idols; and in all his other actions — his movements, his activities, his eating and drinking, his clothing, and all his ways — he will conduct himself with great heaviness, as though all his flesh were lead and all his bones stone or sand.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:126: And another proud man will be found who thinks that, since he is deserving of praise and abundant in merits, he must make the earth tremble, and everyone must quake before him, for it is not fitting that people should presume to speak with him and ask something of him; and if they dare to approach him, he will terrify them with his voice, and with the breath of his lips he will confound them, answering them harshly, his face scowling at every time and every hour.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:127: And there is another proud man who thinks in his heart that he is already so great and honored that honor cannot possibly be separated from him and he has no need of it at all; and to demonstrate this, he does things resembling the deeds of the humble, and goes to an extreme in his conduct to display great lowliness and boundless humility — while his heart is exalted within him, saying: I am so lofty and so honored that I have no need of honor, and all I can do is forgo it, since it is already so abundant with me.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:128: And another proud man will be found who wishes to be greatly noted for his merits and to be distinguished in his ways, to the point that it is not enough for him that the whole world praise him for the merits he thinks he has, but he wants them to add still more to his praise — namely, that he is the humblest of the humble; and so this person becomes proud of his humility, and desires honor precisely for that in which he displays himself as fleeing from it. And such a proud man will place himself below people far lesser than he, or below the most despised of the people, thinking to display thereby the utmost humility, and he will no longer desire any title of greatness and will refuse all elevations, while his heart says within him: there is no one as wise and as humble as I in the whole land.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:129: And indeed, such proud men, even though they outwardly display themselves as humble, cannot avoid pitfalls, for without their knowledge their pride will reveal itself like a flame bursting forth from among potsherds. And the Sages, of blessed memory, have already given a parable for this (Midrash Rabbah, Korach): This may be compared to a house full of straw, in which there were cracks, and the straw kept getting into them; after some days, that straw which was inside those cracks began to come out, and everyone knew that this house was full of straw.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:130: So it is with this matter: they cannot always conceal themselves, and their evil intent will become recognizable through their deeds; but their ways lie in a false humility and a counterfeit lowliness.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:131: And other proud men will be found whose pride remains buried in their hearts, without bringing it out into deed; but they think in their hearts that they are already great sages, knowing matters in their truth, and that not many are as wise as they, and therefore they pay no heed to the words of others, thinking that what is difficult for them will not be easy for others, and that what their own reason shows them so clearly and so simply, they need not concern themselves with the words of those who disagree with them, whether earlier or later authorities, and they have no doubt about their own opinion.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:132: All these are the offshoots of pride, which turns the wise back and makes their knowledge foolish, and removes the heart of the leading sages.
Mesillat Yesharim 11:133: And even students who have not yet fully served their apprenticeship — no sooner have their eyes barely been opened than the sagest of sages already seem, in their own hearts, equal to them.
